brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Three bases in a row: piece:-1,0,0;half-s, piece:0,0,0;half-s, piece:1,0,0;half-s, forming a 3-cell cabinet; open faces capped with caps.
Two drawers fitted on cut faces: drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#0,0#cut (both half-s north cut).
drawer:0#0,0#cut set open=true (pulled open), other drawer closed; visible in 3D view and verified by check_build meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Three half-s bases in a row form the cabinet; two drawers installed on the left and centre cells, centre drawer pulled open (state open=true), right cell remains as cabinet space; caps and joint locking applied and mesh clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three cells, two drawers — one left open. I'll get your cabinet built.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
